title: Non-Adjacent Max Sum
statement:
Pick values from a row so that no two picked positions are neighbours, maximising the total.

Contract
- `values` is a non-null array of non-negative `int`s and may be empty. You choose a set of indices; two chosen indices may never differ by exactly 1.
- Return the largest total of the chosen values. Choosing nothing is allowed, so an empty array gives `0`.
- The total can exceed the `int` range, so return a `long`. Do not mutate `values`.

Examples
- `maxSum(new int[]{4, 1, 7, 3})` returns `11` (indices 0 and 2).
- `maxSum(new int[]{5})` returns `5`.
- `maxSum(new int[]{2, 9, 2})` returns `9`.
hints: Think about one position at a time: either you take it and must skip the previous one, or you leave it.
The best total up to position i depends only on the best totals up to i - 1 and i - 2, so older results never need to be kept.
Carry two running totals (best including/skipping the latest pairing) in `long` variables. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space, where n is the array length.
inputSyntax: Input: the values in brackets or separated by spaces, for example: [4, 1, 7, 3]
